transcript.text: Indesit washer dryer washes fine but the drying cycle doesn't get warm at all, clothes come out cold and wet after 2 hours. Model is XWDE 96 something.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is the heater element. Does it get hot during drying but leave the clothes damp, or is there no heat at all - and were the clothes properly spun before the drying stage?

No heat at all I think - the door glass is stone cold during drying. The drum tumbles and I can hear the fan going, it just never warms up. Not sure about the spin, the washing side seems fine though.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is clean the lint/fluff filter (and condenser filter) and clear the airflow. A blocked lint filter stops the airflow, and many dryers then cut the heat to stop overheating. Clean the fluff filter in the door opening (heat-pump models often have a second one at the bottom too). Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?

I'm not sure about the filter, I haven't checked it yet - I'll have a look now. It's not a heat pump one as far as I know, just the normal condenser type. Heavy use for school uniforms though. Also no burning smell or tripping, in case that matters.

Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]
I haven't actually taken it out yet, I'll go and look now. I can hear water trickling at the back during the dry though, if that helps. Should I do anything else while I'm at it?

You should clean the lint filter and check the condenser unit, as blockages there often prevent proper heating. Ensure the exhaust vent is also clear of debris to allow moist air to escape effectively. Slide the water container out, empty it, check it isn't cracked and that the lid / float is clean, then push it firmly all the way home until it clicks. Was it full or not pushed fully in (and is it sorted), is it cracked, or was it already empty, seated and fine?
Ok, I'll check the water container now. I haven't looked at it yet, so I don't know if it's full or seated properly. It's a condenser type, so I'm not sure there's an exhaust vent to check.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is clean BOTH the lint filter and the deeper condenser/evaporator filters. Some programmes (cool air, refresh, delicates or a low-heat option) dry with little or no heat. Was a cool-air or low-heat programme set (and have you changed it), or was it a normal heat programme?
It was set to standard cotton dry, timed 120 min, so not a cool air one. I haven't changed anything. Last week I did unplug it halfway through a dry to grab a shirt, if that matters.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is blocked airflow tripping the overheat cut-out. Damp laundry is most often an airflow problem, and the first free check is the fluff filter in the door opening — heat-pump models often have a second filter at the bottom too. Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), is the mesh torn, or was it already clean?
